newsitem.title: JAPAN: Albright to discuss China and Korea with Japan.
newsitem.headline: Albright to discuss China and Korea with Japan.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright will hold in-depth talks about China and the Korean Peninsula during her first official visit to Japan on Sunday, government officials said on Friday.
"It's quite probable that a fairly considerable amount of time will be spent discussing China and the situation in the Korean Peninsula," a Japanese foreign ministry official said.

The official said talks between Albright and Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda would likely focus on urging China to maintain the late Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping's reformist line, and also touch on China's entry into the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

She will be the first foreign diplomat to visit China after Deng's death on Thursday. Her spokesman said Albright will shorten her trip to Beijing by one day and leave for Washington before Deng's funeral next Tuesday.

Albright, who will have visited Seoul before arriving in Tokyo on Sunday, is expected to brief Ikeda on the situation in the Korean Peninsula, where tensions have been rising since the recent defection of a senior North Korean official.

On bilateral issues, aside from the confirmation of U.S.-Japan security ties, the two countries will likely touch on the thorny issue of the U.S. military presence in Japan's southern island of Okinawa.

Ikeda, who visited Okinawa this week ahead of Albright's trip, is expected to bring up an incident in which U.S. Marine Corps jets inadvertently fired bullets containing depleted uranium near an island off Okinawa.
Japan-U.S. ties are likely to face further strain in the coming months as 3,000 Okinawan landowners have refused to renew leases due to expire on May 14 for land occupied by U.S. military bases.

Albright will also hold brief talks with trade minister Shinji Sato and defense chief Fumio Kyuma on Sunday and meet Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto over breakfast on Monday before leaving for Beijing.
